paragraphs.title: The Fire, the Sacrifices, and the Temple Dedication

easy.explanation: Fire came down from heaven and consumed the offerings.
easy.q: What came down from heaven after Solomon finished praying?

answers: The burnt offering and the sacrifices
easy.explanation: The fire consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices.
easy.q: What did the fire from heaven consume?

answers: They bowed, worshipped, and praised the LORD
easy.explanation: They bowed themselves with their faces to the ground, worshipped, and praised the LORD.
easy.q: What did the children of Israel do when they saw the fire and the glory of the LORD?

answers: Because the glory of the LORD had filled it
Because the people blocked the entrance
medium.explanation: The glory of the LORD filled the LORD's house.
medium.q: Why could the priests not enter the house of the LORD?

answers: They used musical instruments to praise the LORD
medium.explanation: The Levites served with instruments of musick to praise the LORD.
medium.q: What did the Levites do during the dedication?

medium.explanation: A solemn assembly was a formal gathering of the people.
medium.q: What does the KJV phrase “a solemn assembly” describe?

answers: The court was used for many sacrifices
The people were forbidden to approach the Temple
challenge.explanation: The court was hallowed because burnt offerings and peace offerings were made there.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the middle of the court being hallowed?

answers: The brasen altar could not receive all the offerings
The priests could not find the altar
The people wanted to stay away from the Temple
challenge.explanation: The brasen altar was not able to receive all the burnt offerings, meat offerings, and fat.
challenge.q: Why were sacrifices offered in the court?

answers: Fire from heaven, sacrifices, music, and praise
challenge.explanation: The dedication included heavenly fire, sacrifices, musical praise, and worship.
challenge.q: Which combination best describes the Temple dedication?

paragraphs.title: The Festival of Sukkot and the People's Joy

easy.explanation: The passage says that Solomon kept the feast with all Israel.
The dedication of the altar lasted seven days.
easy.q: How many days did the dedication of the altar last?

easy.explanation: They were sent to their tents glad and merry in heart.
easy.q: How did the people feel when they were sent home?

answers: A very great congregation from all Israel
medium.explanation: All Israel gathered with Solomon as a very great congregation.
medium.q: How large was the congregation at the feast?

medium.explanation: On the eighth day they made a solemn assembly.
medium.q: What happened on the eighth day?

answers: They rejoiced over the goodness the LORD had shown
medium.explanation: They were glad because of the goodness shown by the LORD to David, Solomon, and Israel.
medium.q: Why were the people joyful when they returned home?

answers: The solemn assembly, altar dedication, and feast
Seven days of altar dedication, seven days of the feast, then the solemn assembly
The feast, the solemn assembly, then altar dedication
challenge.explanation: The altar dedication came first, followed by the feast, and then the solemn assembly.
challenge.q: What is the correct order of events?

answers: It covered a very wide area
It gathered beside one small river
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes the broad geographic extent of the gathering.
challenge.q: What does “from the entering in of Hamath unto the river of Egypt” show about the congregation?

challenge.explanation: The passage says that the altar dedication lasted seven days and the feast lasted seven days.
challenge.q: What relationship is shown between the altar dedication and the feast?

paragraphs.title: Solomon Completes His Works and the Lord Responds

answers: The house of the LORD and the king's house
David's house and the priests' house
The people's house and the courthouse
easy.explanation: Solomon finished the house of the LORD and the king's house.
easy.q: Which two buildings did Solomon finish?

easy.explanation: The LORD appeared to Solomon by night.
easy.q: When did the LORD appear to Solomon?

easy.explanation: The LORD chose the place for an house of sacrifice.
easy.q: For what purpose did the LORD choose the place?

medium.explanation: The LORD promised to hear from heaven, forgive their sin, and heal their land.
medium.q: What did the LORD promise to do if His people humbled themselves, prayed, sought His face, and turned from their wicked ways?

answers: The building of the king's house
The LORD's judgment in response to the people's condition
medium.explanation: The LORD said that He could shut up heaven so that there would be no rain.
medium.q: What could cause the rain to stop according to the LORD's words?

answers: They must submit themselves before God
medium.explanation: The phrase means to humble or submit oneself before God.
medium.q: What does “shall humble themselves” mean in this passage?

answers: Prayer, sin, and leaving the land
Humility, prayer, seeking God's face, and turning from wicked ways
Building a Temple, fighting, and crowning a king
challenge.explanation: The LORD names humility, prayer, seeking His face, and repentance.
challenge.q: Which sequence describes the way to restoration presented by the LORD?

answers: The Temple is associated with God's attention to prayer
The Temple is only a residence for priests
The Temple must always remain closed
challenge.explanation: The LORD says that He will attend to the prayer made in that place.
challenge.q: What is meant by the LORD's eyes being open and His ears being attentive in this place?

answers: After Solomon completes the work, the LORD appears and confirms the Temple as a place of sacrifice and prayer
The completed work begins Israel's exile
challenge.explanation: After the buildings are completed, the LORD appears to Solomon and confirms His choice of the house.

paragraphs.title: The Covenant Conditions and the Continuation of David's Dynasty

easy.explanation: The LORD told Solomon to walk before Him as David his father walked.
easy.q: Whose way was Solomon commanded to walk in?

easy.explanation: Solomon was to observe the LORD's statutes and judgments.
The LORD promised to establish the throne of Solomon's kingdom.
easy.q: What did the LORD promise to establish for Solomon?

answers: That Solomon obey the LORD and walk in David's way
medium.explanation: The promise depended on Solomon's obedience and faithful walk.
medium.q: What was the condition attached to the LORD's promise to Solomon?

medium.explanation: The LORD referred to the covenant He had made with David.
medium.q: What did the promise concerning the throne refer back to?

answers: There would be no ruler or heir from Solomon's line
No trees would be cut in the Temple
The city gates would never close
medium.explanation: The statement concerns the continuation of a ruler from David's line.
medium.q: What does “There shall not fail thee a man to be ruler in Israel” mean?

answers: Obedience is connected with the stability of the kingdom
The promise is given only if the people abandon God's commandments
challenge.explanation: The LORD links Solomon's obedience with establishing his royal throne.
challenge.q: What connection is shown between the LORD's command and His promise?

answers: The reference to the covenant with David
The reference to the altar dedication
challenge.explanation: The LORD specifically mentions His covenant with David.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the promise was part of an earlier covenant?

answers: The Temple's independence from the king's conduct
challenge.explanation: Both expressions stress complete and ongoing obedience.
challenge.q: What do “do according to all that I have commanded thee” and “observe my statutes and my judgments” emphasize?

paragraphs.title: The Warning of Destruction and Its Explanation

easy.explanation: The warning concerns turning away from the LORD's statutes and commandments.
The passage warns that they might serve and worship other gods.
easy.q: Whom might the people serve instead of the LORD?

answers: It would become a proverb and a byword
It would become the king's private house
easy.explanation: The LORD said He would make the house a proverb and a byword.
easy.q: What could happen to the house sanctified for the LORD's name?

answers: They would be plucked up from the land
medium.explanation: The LORD warned that He would pluck them up by the roots out of His land.
medium.q: What could happen to Israel if the people forsook the LORD's commandments and served other gods?

answers: Why hath the LORD done thus unto this land, and unto this house?
medium.explanation: They would ask why the LORD had done this to the land and the house.
medium.q: What would passersby ask about the ruined house?

medium.explanation: The ruined house would become a public example of judgment and warning.
medium.q: What does “a proverb and a byword” mean in this context?

answers: The people forsook the LORD, served other gods, worshipped them, and served them
The priests did not know how to sing
challenge.explanation: The destruction would be explained as the result of abandoning the LORD and serving other gods.
challenge.q: What explanation would be given for the destruction?

answers: Forsaking the LORD and serving idols leads to all this evil
The people's joy leads to the Temple's destruction
challenge.explanation: The passage says that this evil came because the people forsook the LORD and served other gods.
challenge.q: Which cause-and-effect relationship appears in these verses?

answers: The warning includes both the people in the land and the Temple
The land was unrelated to the people's conduct
challenge.explanation: The judgment concerns both Israel's removal from the land and the casting away of the sanctified house.
challenge.q: Why is it significant that both the land and the house are mentioned in the judgment?
